short: A swift Swedish preemptive strike against Denmark-Norway that secured strategic supremacy.
full:
Initiated by Swedish Field Marshal Lennart Torstensson on orders from Axel Oxenstierna, the war began with a sudden invasion of Holstein and Jutland in December 1643. Sweden aimed to eliminate Danish threats to its supply lines and end the toll extracted at the Sound. Danish forces, caught off-guard, were unable to mount a cohesive defense. A subsequent Swedish naval victory at Fehmarn in 1644 shattered the Danish fleet.

The conflict concluded swiftly with the Treaty of Brömsebro in 1645. Denmark was forced to cede significant territories, including Jämtland, Härjedalen, Gotland, and Saaremaa, alongside a temporary hold on Halland. This decisive outcome effectively dismantled Danish dominance in the Baltic, elevating Sweden to the preeminent power in Northern Europe and paving the way for its imperial golden age.
